source.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
source.authors: Adam Karvonen; C. Rager; Johnny Lin; Curt Tigges; J. Bloom; David Chanin; Yeu-Tong Lau; Eoin Farrell; Callum McDougall; K. Ayonrinde; Demian Till; M. Wearden; Arthur Conmy; Samuel Marks; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: It reports a RAVEL evaluation result comparing latent interventions with and without the SAE reconstruction-error term, a different measure from the original dark-matter analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper does not analyze whether SAE error is linearly predictable, how error norms scale across SAE sizes, or whether SAE replacement is worse than matched random errors. Its reported loss-recovered metric compares SAE reconstruction with zero ablation, not matched random errors. The RAVEL error-term comparison is the only reported result directly bearing on a claim version.
record.test_reason: SAEBench is a benchmark of SAE architectures. It never measures dark matter: no linear predictability of error, no per-token error-norm scaling, no matched random-error comparison, and no linear/nonlinear split. The only error-term result is a brief implementation note in Appendix D. There, adding the reconstruction error back into RAVEL interventions lowered Cause and Disentangle scores, so the authors omit it for RAVEL. That measures how well a latent intervention transfers attributes, which is a related but different construct. It does not measure how much of the model's behaviour a feature-based analysis loses without the error term (V5). The study uses the error term as a tool (it is added back in SCR/TPP) without testing the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE quality involves trade-offs across metrics, and that sparsity-fidelity gains do not reliably translate into downstream performance. Matryoshka SAEs excel at disentanglement despite slightly worse reconstruction, larger dictionaries improve reconstruction and interpretability but degrade concept isolation, and moderate L0 (50-150) is a reasonable compromise. The RAVEL error-term remark is an implementation choice: the error term is omitted for RAVEL but added back for SCR/TPP to avoid destabilizing effects. It is not a conclusion about dark matter.
record.recipe_differences: The study benchmarks SAE architectures across multiple metrics; it does not use the original dark-matter decomposition or matched random-error comparison. Its RAVEL comparison concerns whether to retain the reconstruction-error term during latent interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: RAVEL scores depend on whether the SAE reconstruction-error term is incorporated; the text reports an approximately 0.02 Disentangle reduction in many cases.

fits_no_version.finding: In RAVEL, adding the SAE reconstruction error back after a latent intervention lowered Cause and Disentangle scores, often reducing Disentangle by about 0.02 (Appendix D). The authors therefore omit the error term for RAVEL but keep it for SCR/TPP, so changes stay confined to the targeted latents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether keeping the SAE error term during latent attribute-transfer interventions helps or hurts intervention success and disentanglement.

record.problems: The reconstruction-error comparison is reported briefly without model, SAE size, exact score values, uncertainty, or a quantitative Cause-score difference. The paper does not directly evaluate the other dark-matter claims.
record.rows_left_out: Loss Recovered results and SAE architecture/width comparisons were not extracted as rows: they do not compare matched random errors or measure the stated dark-matter properties. The benchmark results are reported in Figures 2–23 and related text.

untested.parts: All: no regression of SAE error on input activations.
All: no per-token error-norm prediction or cross-size failure overlap. Loss Recovered rises with width (Fig. 3, Appendix I), but this is not reported as an error-scaling or non-vanishing analysis.
All: Loss Recovered is compared with zero ablation only, never with matched random errors.
Whether circuits or steering analyses lose model behaviour when the error term is omitted; not measured.

Architectures differ on Loss Recovered (ReLU worst, TopK/BatchTopK best at low L0), but error is not decomposed into dark-matter components. Whether dark matter shrinks with architecture is not analysed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its 'challenges V5' label are not supported; the single row is a one-sentence implementation note measuring a different construct. Loss Recovered by width and architecture (Figs. 2, 3, 6, 12-23) is reported only in figures. It concerns overall reconstruction fidelity relative to zero ablation, not dark-matter structure, so it is left out, as the record declares.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of input activations.
Per-token error-norm predictability, overlap of failure contexts across SAE sizes, and whether error vanishes with scale.
Whether SAE replacement harms loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether the linear and nonlinear error components differ in the proposed ways or respond differently to dictionary learning.
The paper tests the reconstruction-error term in RAVEL interventions, but not circuits or steering analyses generally, nor the share of model behavior those analyses lose.
Whether SAE error is mostly caused by training objectives or architectures, and whether it shrinks with better architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Omitted the SAE reconstruction-error term from RAVEL latent interventions; the comparison condition incorporated the term.
rows.baseline: With the SAE reconstruction-error term incorporated; score not stated
rows.value: Omitting the error term yielded higher Cause and Disentangle scores; incorporating it frequently reduced Disentangle by approximately 0.02
rows.note: The text gives an approximate reduction for Disentangle; it does not quantify the Cause-score change.
rows.check: RAVEL Cause/Disentangle scores measure whether an intervention on SAE latents transfers one attribute cleanly. They do not measure what share of model behaviour is lost when the error term is dropped, so they cannot show V5's effect. The record's 'reversed' state reads V5 as 'keeping the error improves intervention scores', which V5 does not claim. A lower Cause score with the error added back is expected, since the untouched error term retains original-entity information. No model, width or exact values are given. Moved to fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Error retention is an evaluation technique. The RAVEL comparison measures intervention success and disentanglement, not the share of original model behaviour carried by the error.

tranche.reason: The benchmark retains reconstruction error in SCR and TPP to isolate latent interventions, but reports benchmark performance rather than testing any dark-matter claim version.

source_check.notes: Adding the error term reduced both RAVEL Cause and Disentangle scores; Disentangle frequently decreased by approximately 0.02. No numerical Cause-score change or model-specific breakdown is stated for this comparison.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: In this evaluation, incorporating rather than omitting the reconstruction-error term lowered the reported scores, contrary to the claim that keeping the term preserves a meaningful share of behavior (r1).
